isolation: firejail child process (NOT vm2 — vm2 is deprecated). Linux timeout enforces wall-clock limit.
require_rule: require() ONLY the modules above. require("fs"|"child_process"|"http"...) is blocked.

v1.memory: HIGH — loads all upstream node data into the child process
v1.use_when: Need full workflow context / historical node data / loop helpers

v2.constraint: Accessing $ or $item THROWS (intentionally not exposed). Inputs must be declared via the node input-mapping; resolved values arrive as $input.<key>.
v2.memory: MINIMAL — only declared inputs passed in
v2.use_when: Simple transforms / perf-critical / only need specific inputs (preferred default for new nodes)

versions.selector: is_code_node_v2 flag on the node decides v1 vs v2.

return: Return a plain object; it becomes this node's execution_data for downstream nodes. Returning undefined/null is treated as "Return data is missing." error.

zuper_api_recipe.note: Calling a Zuper API from a code/http node: the worker does NOT auto-inject Zuper auth. Auth header = 'x-api-key': variable.zuper_api_key (NOT Bearer). Base = the company DC (e.g. https://<dc>.zuperpro.com/api). The workflow MUST have a `zuper_api_key` variable — create it (create_variable, is_sensitive:true) or return a clarification; never invent variable.zuper_dc_base/zuper_bearer.
zuper_api_recipe.http_vs_code_url: CODE node: `variable.zuper_dc_base` inside the JS is fine (plain string at runtime). http_request_v2 node: the `url` field is validated with new URL() at SAVE → it MUST be a LITERAL absolute URL (e.g. http://localhost:4500/api/jobs/filter or https://<dc>.zuperpro.com/api/...). NEVER put `{{ variable }}` in the http `url` — `{{ variable.zuper_dc_base }}/jobs/filter` => 'Invalid URL'. Only field VALUES like the x-api-key header may be a {{ variable }} expression.
zuper_api_recipe.get_by_uid: GET {dc}/api/jobs/{job_uid}  (single record) — prefer the native zuper_get_record node over a code/http call.
zuper_api_recipe.list_filter: FILTERED LIST endpoint = **POST {dc}/api/{module}/filter** (jobs → POST {dc}/api/jobs/filter). NOT `/jobs/list_v2` (that 404s 'Cannot POST' on this backend) and NOT `/jobs/meta/filter` (schema only). Body: { page:1, count:10, filter_rules:[ RULE, … ], filter_rule_operator:'AND' }. **ALWAYS use count:10** (never 50/100/1000) — the record total is unknown, so paginate via the loop pattern (see `pagination_pattern`) instead of a big page size. A RULE = { key, operator, value, type:'default_field', module:'JOB' } — for a *_uid lookup use type:'nested_field',field_type:'LOOKUP'; for a custom field use key:'cf_<uuid>',type:'custom_field',field_type:'<TYPE>'. Real keys come from describe_trigger_filters('JOB') / zuper_dc_get('/jobs/meta/filter') — NEVER invent a key (no `date`, no `scheduled_date_range`). DATES use operator:'BETWEEN' with value:[fromISO,toISO] (compute the range yourself — there is NO `rangeKey`).
zuper_api_recipe.pagination_pattern: FETCH-ALL of UNKNOWN COUNT → paginate with count:10 + a loop. Topology: trigger → http(fetch PAGE 1, count:10, filters) → code('compute pages' from page-1 total) → loop(input_data = the page array) → [BODY: http(fetch CURRENT page, count:10, same filters)] → code('aggregate' page-1 + every loop page, build body) → action. WIRING: the loop BODY is ONLY the per-page fetch (loop --two-b--> fetch; fetch --loopEdge--> loop). The 'aggregate' code node + everything after run AFTER the loop, on its EXIT handle (loop --two-a--> aggregate --one-a--> action) — NEVER inside the body (aggregate must NOT have a loopEdge back to the loop; it runs once, post-loop, and reads all pages via $.getNodeData). The page-1 response carries the total — `body.total_records` (or `total`/`total_count`) and sometimes `total_pages`/`current_page`. Use count:10 everywhere; NEVER hardcode a big count. See compute_pages / loop_input_data / paginate_child_fetch / paginate_aggregate.
zuper_api_recipe.loop_input_data: The loop node's REQUIRED `input_data` field (EXPRESSION) = the array to iterate, i.e. the page array from the compute node: `{{ $.getLatestNodeData('compute pages').data.pages }}`. A loop SHIPS BLANK and never iterates unless you set input_data. Inside the body, the current element is `$item` → its page number is `{{ $item.data.page }}`.
zuper_api_recipe.status_type_enum: Valid `current_job_status.status_type` values: NEW, SCHEDULED, ON_MY_WAY, STARTED, ON_HOLD, COMPLETED, CANNOT_COMPLETE, CANCELED, FAILED, PAID, CLOSED, FOLLOW_UP, FOLLOW_UP_SAME_JOB, OTHER. (IN_PROGRESS→STARTED; INCOMPLETE→CANNOT_COMPLETE; CANCELLED→CANCELED — there is NO 'INCOMPLETE'.) For 'completed AND un-completed', do NOT filter by status — fetch ALL (date filter only) and split by status_type==='COMPLETED' in the code/branch node.
zuper_api_recipe.timezone_dates: CRITICAL: 'today'/'this week' is the COMPANY's local day, NOT UTC. A raw `new Date()` computes a UTC day → it MISSES jobs scheduled in the local evening (the #1 '0 results' bug). ALWAYS compute date windows in the company timezone with `require('moment-timezone')` + `variable.company_timezone` (an IANA string like 'Asia/Calcutta', auto-provisioned by the builder; default 'UTC' if absent): `const m=require('moment-timezone'); const tz=variable.company_timezone||'UTC'; const start_iso=m.tz(tz).startOf('day').toISOString(); const end_iso=m.tz(tz).endOf('day').toISOString();`. The filter `value:[start_iso,end_iso]` is then correct for the company's day.
zuper_api_recipe.http_body_referencing_dates: When an http_request_v2 fetch node uses dates computed by an upstream 'compute date range' code node, the http `json_body` (an EXPRESSION field) references that node's output — DO NOT compute dates in the http field (no Nunjucks `.date()`/`new Date()`; those FAIL). Example json_body value (replace 'Compute date range' with the real node name): `{"page":1,"count":100,"filter_rules":[{"key":"scheduled_start_time","operator":"BETWEEN","value":["{{ $.getLatestNodeData('Compute date range').data.start_iso }}","{{ $.getLatestNodeData('Compute date range').data.end_iso }}"],"type":"default_field","module":"JOB"}],"filter_rule_operator":"AND"}`. The x-api-key header stays `{{ variable.zuper_api_key }}`.
